bugs: A guest request to /api/posts without an `Accept: application/json` header returns 500 (Route [login] not defined) instead of 401. bootstrap/app.php was never set up to make guests on api/* get a 401 or to render exceptions as JSON.

Empty query filters (`?status=&tag=&per_page=`) return 422 because ConvertEmptyStringsToNull turns them into null and the rules are `sometimes` without `nullable` (app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:14-16). A client that sends a blank filter gets an error instead of an unfiltered list.
antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:36: `->response()->setStatusCode(201)` is unnecessary ceremony. JsonResource already returns 201 when the model was just created (`wasRecentlyCreated`).
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:43: checks `$request->has('tags')` on raw input but then reads validated data. `$request->safe()->has('tags')` would be consistent.
app/Policies/PostPolicy.php:17: delete() repeats update()'s logic instead of delegating to it (trivial).
tests/Feature/PostApiTest.php:206: the draft status filter is checked through a direct model scope query, not the HTTP endpoint.
Store and update run multiple writes (post plus tag sync) with no transaction (app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:33-34, 41-44); impl-2 shares this.
strengths: Uses `$request->enum('status', PostStatus::class)` and `$request->integer('per_page', 15)`, which are nice typed request helpers.
Modern model attributes: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope], a casts() method and an enum cast.
An observer handles slug generation and setting published_at on publish; the policy is enforced with route `->can()`, so non-authors get 403 before validation runs.
Tag syncing is a clean collection pipeline (trim, filter, uniqueStrict, firstOrCreate) that silently de-duplicates.
Index eager-loads tags, uses whereRelation for the tag filter, has a stable latest()/latest('id') order, and calls withQueryString.

antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:20: `PostStatus::from($status)` is done by hand where `$request->enum('status', PostStatus::class)` would be the idiomatic helper. Line 24 likewise uses `?? 15` instead of `$request->integer()`.
Store and update run multiple writes (post plus tag sync) with no transaction (app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:32-33, 40-44).
app/Observers/PostObserver.php:14: the default status is set in the observer (`??=`) even though the migration already has a column default. A model `$attributes` default would be more conventional.
tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php from the base app was deleted, which is unnecessary churn.
routes/api.php:9: only PUT is registered (no PATCH), even though update accepts partial `sometimes` payloads. impl-1 has the same gap.
strengths: bootstrap/app.php sets redirectGuestsTo plus shouldRenderJsonWhen for api/*, so guests get a JSON 401 even without an Accept header (verified by probe; impl-1 returns 500).
Index filters are `nullable`, so blank filter parameters are treated as no filter (tested), and per_page is bounded.
`distinct:ignore_case` on tags.* plus trim/unique in syncTags; createOrFirst is race-safe against the unique tag-name index.
Store returns a bare PostResource and relies on the automatic 201; Model::shouldBeStrict is enabled outside production.
Policy enforced through route `->can()` with slug binding, and a test confirms a non-author gets 403 even when the body is invalid.

Thorough tests: plain guest 401, ignoring a client-supplied slug/user_id/published_at, keeping vs clearing tags, keeping published_at across draft→publish, pagination meta, and validation of the index query string.
A composite index (user_id, status, created_at) matches the index query.

v.rationale: Both implementations use nearly the same structure: an enum cast, an observer for the slug and published_at, a policy enforced through route `can()`, form requests, a resource, and scopes defined with #[Scope]. All tests pass in both (impl-2: 23, impl-1: 22). Probes found the differences. impl-1 returns a 500 when a guest calls the API without an `Accept: application/json` header, because bootstrap/app.php still redirects guests to a `login` route that doesn't exist. impl-1 also rejects blank filter parameters with a 422. impl-2 handles both cases correctly and has tests for them. impl-2's validation is also stricter (case-insensitive distinct tags, nullable index filters), it turns on strict mode, it relies on the automatic 201 instead of setting the status code by hand, and its tests cover more edge cases. impl-1 does use the typed request helpers `enum()` and `integer()` slightly better. Neither wraps the post write and tag sync in a transaction, and neither registers PATCH. Overall impl-2 ranks first.
